the basolater‐ al amygdala is necessary for learning about the sensory‐specific aspects of a reinforcer and the central amygd-ala is responsible for learning about the reinforcing value of a stimulus.
the basolater‐ al amygdala is responsible for learning about the specific properties of a rewarding event and for choosing between rewards based on the relative value of those rewards.
the basolater‐ al and central amygdalae are responsible for learning different aspects of reward‐related learning and extinction.

the neural basis of reward‐related learning, and the role of the central and basolateral amyg‐ dala in this process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amygdala is important for learning about specific rewarding events, but is less important for learning about the general reinforcing properties of those events.

the basolatal amygdala plays a critical role in learning to choose between specific rewards based upon their specific sensory properties, whereas the central amygdal plays a critical role for learning the general reinforcement value of events, and for the regulation of motivation.

the amygdala has a critical role in the acquisition of reward‐related learning, and that it is also involved in the extinction of reward‐associated behaviours.
